procedure.description: septoplasty with or without cartilage scoring, contouring, or replacement with graft

denial.text: Silverline Medicare Advantage denied the claim for CPT 30520 (septoplasty with or without cartilage scoring, contouring, or replacement with graft) with date of service 2026-06-14. CARC 167: This (these) diagnosis(es) is (are) not covered. Payer remark: The diagnosis reported (chronic rhinitis) is not a covered indication for this procedure.

criteria.text: Nasal airway obstruction symptoms persisting for at least 3 months.
Failure of at least 4 weeks of an intranasal corticosteroid together with an oral or intranasal antihistamine.
Physical examination or imaging documenting septal deviation obstructing the nasal airway, with symptoms not explained by mucosal disease alone.

chart.text: Called his with the cholesterol results. Total 202, LDL 157, HDL 52, triglycerides 134. Discussed diet and walking. He wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
From the referring physician: please evaluate for surgical management. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.
Blood pressure check. 123 over 72 today, 122 over 75 on repeat. He has been taking the lisinopril 20 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 12 weeks.

23 year old man here for nasal obstruction. Broke the nose playing ball as a teenager, never fixed. Discussed septoplasty, possible turbinate reduction, recovery of a week or so. His history otherwise: mild asthma, albuterol maybe twice a year. Surgeries: a knee scope. Allergies: penicillin, rash. Never smoked, occasional beer, has three kids at home. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Cannot breathe through the right side for going on 12 months, mouth-breathes at night, his spouse says the snoring is worse. He has been on fluticasone two sprays each side daily plus loratadine since his PCP started them, says it does nothing for the right side. Anterior rhinoscopy: septum deviated to the right with a caudal spur contacting the inferior turbinate, right airway maybe 29 percent of the left. Turbinates decongest fine with oxymetazoline, the right side does not open up.
Vitamin D came back 19. Started 2000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.

Here with a cough and congestion for 9 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if he gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
CT sinus without contrast: rightward septal deviation with a bony spur abutting the right inferior turbinate, no significant sinus disease, no polyps.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 18 and 18. No ocular pathology noted.

Follow-up on the nose. Reviewed the imaging with him. Still wants to proceed. Vitals today 112 over 79, pulse 88. 6 weeks on the fluticasone and loratadine now, used it every day per him, no change in the right sided obstruction.

Mole on the left forearm that his spouse noticed. About 5 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change he is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.
He called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in the spring. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.
Message from the patient about scheduling. Wants a date in the next couple of months if the insurance comes through. Passed to the surgery scheduler.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 10 years.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, he will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the right for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.
Follow-up. Same story, no better. He asked about timing around work and family, we talked through it. Still wants to proceed.
Patient called about a tick bite on the shoulder after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.
Work note requested for a sick day last Monday. Faxed to the employer.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 1.3, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 75. Repeat in a year.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.

Knee pain going down stairs, left side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.
Pre-op. Consent signed, septoplasty with possible inferior turbinate reduction. No aspirin for ten days.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 167 denial can be answered from the record.
